original_question: For a group word w(x1,..., xn) on n letters, define e0(x1,..., xn) = x1 and ek+1(x1,..., xn) = w(ek(x1,..., xn),..., xn) for all k ∈ N. A group G is said to satisfy the Engel type iterated identity w if for all x1,..., xn ∈ G there exists m ∈ N such that em(x1,..., xn) = 1. Conjecture: For every non-trivial word w, if a finitely generated branch group G(see 15.12) satisfies the iterated identity w, then G is a torsion group. This is true in the case of the commutator word w = [x1, x2 ] (G. Fernández- Alcober, M. Noce, G. Tracey, J. Algebra, 554(2020), 54–77).

refined_question: Let w=w(x1,...,xn) be a nontrivial word in the free group on x1,...,xn. For k≥0 define e0(x1,...,xn)=x1 and e_{k+1}(x1,...,xn)=w(e_k(x1,...,xn),x2,...,xn). Say that a group G satisfies the Engel-type iterated identity w if for every x1,...,xn∈G there exists m=m(x1,...,xn)∈N such that e_m(x1,...,xn)=1. Suppose G is a finitely generated branch group in the sense that G acts faithfully and level-transitively on a rooted tree T, for each vertex v the rigid vertex stabilizer consists of elements acting trivially outside the subtree T_v, the n-th rigid level stabilizer is generated by the rigid vertex stabilizers of vertices at level n, and every rigid level stabilizer has finite index in G. Must G be a torsion group? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
